subject: Meta-reg kickoff — few-shot learning without the task-design tax
body:
Hi team,

Kicking off the meta-regularization project. The problem it solves: most meta-learning algorithms implicitly require meta-training tasks to be mutually exclusive — think per-task random shuffling of class-to-label assignments — or the learner memorizes a single zero-shot solution and never adapts. Our published meta-regularization objective, built on information theory, puts precedence on data-driven adaptation instead, so users stop hand-designing task tricks. Two vision teams currently maintain exactly those brittle label-shuffling pipelines.

Milestones (short window, closes 04-20):
- 02-27: reference implementation reproducing the paper's non-mutually-exclusive benchmark results.
- 03-20: meta-reg objective packaged as a drop-in for our few-shot training library.
- 04-13: A/B on one vision team's pipeline; go/no-go for wider rollout in the next window.

Bao owns staffing; Freya is TL.

Lucia
